summary: trunc removes a number’s fractional portion, moving toward zero.
documentation: trunc removes a number’s fractional portion, moving toward zero. This differs from floor for negative values and from rounding to the nearest integer.
returns: Its integer part, represented as a Number.
caution: Bitwise integer conversions can overflow at 32 bits and are not equivalent. JSON represents negative zero as ordinary zero.
scenarios: Display only completed whole units from a measured quantity.
Strip fractional parts from a temporary numeric preview.
Compare signed integer portions of imported measurements.
title: Keep the signed whole portion
problem: Input is a finite number inside the safe-integer range. Return its whole portion by discarding the fractional part toward zero. Treat a result of negative zero as JSON zero.
goal: Use Math.trunc() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use trunc, not floor: -3.8 should become -3.
